# Fourier Series

A periodic signal can be decomposed into a sum of sinusoids at integer multiples of a fundamental frequency. The coefficients are found by projecting the signal onto each basis function. Orthogonality of the basis is what makes this projection well-defined: the inner product of two distinct basis functions is zero, so each coefficient depends only on its own basis function.

## Convergence

The series converges to the signal at points of continuity. At a jump discontinuity it converges to the midpoint of the jump. Near a discontinuity the partial sums overshoot; this is the Gibbs phenomenon and the overshoot does not vanish as more terms are added.

## Practical use

In practice the transform is computed on sampled data using the FFT, which reduces the cost from quadratic to N log N.

# Reasonable Accommodation

Employers must provide reasonable accommodation to employees with disabilities unless doing so imposes undue hardship. Accommodation is assessed case by case. Undue hardship considers cost relative to the employer's resources, not to the individual role.

## Process

The employee makes a request. The employer engages in an interactive process. Documentation may be requested but must be limited to what establishes the need.

## Common accommodations

Flexible hours, assistive software, modified workstations, and written rather than verbal instructions.
